title: Draw the frame: a recursive call
prompt:
The program is paused two calls deep in `sum_to`: `main` called `sum_to(4)`, which called `sum_to(3)`. Draw the running call's frame.

Every call to `sum_to` builds a frame of its own with the same layout, and fp points at the frame of the call that is running. Three frames are on the stack at the pause; draw the newest one, in bytes from its fp.

## What is checked

- the frame's size in bytes
- the offsets from fp of `n_s` and `part_s`
- the offsets from fp of the saved fp and the saved lr

Check runs the program to the pause and compares each number with the frame the emulator draws there. A wrong number shows a hint, never the answer.
program:
// Add 1 + 2 + ... + n with a function that calls itself.

define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(n_r, w19)

n_size = 4                                      // int
part_size = 8                                   // long

n_s = 16
part_s = (n_s + n_size + 7) & -8                // a long starts on a multiple of 8
alloc = -(part_s + part_size) & -16
dealloc = -alloc

.data
fmt_out:    .string "sum to %d = %ld\n"

.text

// sum_to(w0 = n) -> x0 = 1 + 2 + ... + n
        .balign 4
        .global sum_to
sum_to:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, alloc]!
        mov     fp, sp

        str     w0, [fp, n_s]                   // n has to outlive the call below
        str     xzr, [fp, part_s]               // nothing added yet
        cmp     w0, 1
        b.le    st_base                         // sum_to(1) is 1

        sub     w0, w0, 1
        bl      sum_to                          // x0 = sum_to(n - 1)
        str     x0, [fp, part_s]
        ldrsw   x9, [fp, n_s]
        ldr     x10, [fp, part_s]
        add     x0, x10, x9                     // n + sum_to(n - 1)
        b       st_done
st_base:
        ldrsw   x0, [fp, n_s]                   // n itself
st_done:
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], dealloc
        ret

        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        mov     n_r, 4
        mov     w0, n_r
        bl      sum_to                          // x0 = sum_to(4)

        mov     x2, x0
        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     w1, n_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret

slots.name: n_s
slots.hint: n_s is given as a plain number in the program, and it is the same in every call.

slots.name: part_s
slots.hint: Work out (n_s + n_size + 7) & -8 with n_s = 16 and n_size = 4.

hints.size: Every call to sum_to makes the same frame. Add up to the end of part_s (part_s + part_size), then round up to a multiple of 16.
hints.savedFp: The running call's stp put its caller's fp at its own new sp, and mov fp, sp points fp there.
hints.savedLr: In every call's frame the saved lr comes right after the saved fp, as the stp stores them.
